SourceProvenance.description:
Where a governed memory source came from and under what authority.

Every field is a reference. Nothing here carries memory content: this records *which* fact a bundle rested on, not what the fact said.

authority_ref.description: What authorized its use here — typically a `memory_residency_policy` reference. Recorded, never authenticated here.

memory_ref.description: The memory fact, in forge_contract_core reference grammar: `<artifact_family>:<artifact_id>:v<artifact_version>`.

bundle_hash.description: SHA-256 over the same canonical string the legacy digest covers.

context_bundle_id.description:
Algorithm-tagged: `ctxb.sha256.<64 hex>`.

The tag is the point. An untagged identity cannot say which function produced it, so a resolver holding a mixed population has to guess — and the guess is only safe while exactly one algorithm has ever been used, which is the assumption this slice exists to remove.

legacy_context_bundle_id.description:
The FNV-1a 64 identity this bundle would have had before Slice 39, and still has wherever it was already recorded.

Not deprecated dead weight: `context_packs` in DataForge keys on the id and has no retention — no `DELETE`, no TTL, no cleanup job — so rows minted under the old scheme never age out. Resolution across both forms is therefore permanent rather than transitional, and a consumer needs this value to find a pack stored before the change.
